title: Pause, crash, resume: supersteps, checkpoints and durable hosting
brief: An approval can take two days, and the host will restart in between. Decide what gets saved, where it is stored, what must be rebuilt identically on resume, and which long-running feature you are really using. The dials are not given.

steps.title: Collect
steps.md: Pending messages from the last superstep are gathered.

steps.title: Route
steps.md: Messages travel along edges: direct, conditional, switch-case, fan-out or fan-in.

steps.title: Barrier
steps.md: The step waits for the slowest executor. A writer sees its own shared-state update at once, others see it next superstep.

steps.title: Checkpoint
steps.md: Executor state, pending messages, pending requests and responses, and shared state are saved. Then new messages are queued.

blocks.md: The model is modified Pregel (bulk synchronous parallel). It gives a deterministic order and clean checkpoint boundaries, and it has a cost: a fan-out where one branch is a chain and another is a single slow executor stalls the chain at the barrier [[r6]]. Python 1.13.0 (2026-07-30) also writes an entry checkpoint before the first superstep and when request responses arrive [[r7]].

blocks.title: A human request across a restart
blocks.alt: The workflow saves a checkpoint holding a pending request and emits a request_info event. The host restarts. The user's answer arrives with a checkpoint id, the workflow loads the checkpoint, re-emits the request and applies the response.
blocks.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant W as Workflow
  participant S as Checkpoint store
  W->>S: save checkpoint with pending request
  W-->>U: request_info event
  Note over W: host restarts, hours pass
  U->>W: run with checkpoint id and responses
  W->>S: load checkpoint
  W->>W: re-emit request, apply response
blocks.caption: Pending requests live in the checkpoint and are re-emitted on restore. You can pass `checkpoint_id` and `responses` to `workflow.run` in one call [[r8]]. Topic w11-t16.

blocks.takeaway: Storage is a threat-model choice as much as a durability choice. For waits of days the question moves from where the checkpoint lives to what wakes the run, which is what the Durable Extension adds (Beta in Python and preview in .NET as of 2026-10-13).

What it is

The provider holds the run. Your process holds only the token

A parent delegates tasks to named child agents through six tools. Task status is `running`, `completed`, `failed` or `lost`. There is no cancel tool, results return as text and child approvals are not proxied

blocks.title: Failure modes on the road to resume

items.symptom: A rebuilt workflow will not resume, or resumes into the wrong executor.
items.cause: Topology or executor identities changed. In .NET the agents lacked a stable `ChatClientAgentOptions.Id` or the `Name` moved.
items.fix: Pin ids and names, treat the graph as versioned, and test a restore in CI [[r7]].

items.symptom: After an upgrade, old checkpoints fail to load a custom class.
items.cause: File storage (since 2026-04-09) and Cosmos storage (since 2026-04-21) use a restricted unpickler that rejects types you have not allowed.
items.fix: List the type in `allowed_checkpoint_types=["module:qualname"]`, or write a custom storage. Module-level functions stay rejected.

items.symptom: Independent paths run slower than the slowest branch alone.
items.cause: The superstep barrier holds a chain until the slow executor in the same step finishes.
items.fix: Merge the steps of an independent path into one executor.

items.symptom: Tests that count or order checkpoints break after an upgrade.
items.cause: Python 1.13.0 (2026-07-30) added entry checkpoints, so counts and order changed.
items.fix: Assert on resume behaviour, not on checkpoint counts.

items.symptom: A user's approval starts a new run instead of continuing the old one.
items.cause: The answer was sent without the pending request or checkpoint it belongs to.
items.fix: Resume with `workflow.run(responses=...)`, passing `checkpoint_id` in the same call after a restart [[r8]].

quiz.q: After a deploy, a workflow resumed from a file checkpoint fails to load a custom dataclass held in executor state. Nothing else changed. What is the most likely cause and fix?
options: The restricted unpickler rejects unlisted types: add the type to `allowed_checkpoint_types` or use a custom storage
Checkpoints are written only at workflow entry, so the executor state was never saved
File storage cannot hold executor state at all, so move everything to in-memory storage and accept losing it on restart
The superstep barrier discarded the dataclass, so add a fan-in edge before the executor
quiz.explain: File storage has used a restricted unpickler since python-1.0.1 (2026-04-09), so types outside the allowed list fail to load, and `allowed_checkpoint_types` or custom storage is the documented way out. Checkpoints are written at every superstep end, file storage does hold executor state, and the barrier controls timing, not what is serialized.

quiz.q: A fan-out starts two branches in the same superstep. Branch A is a chain of three executors that take 2 s each. Branch B is one executor that takes 9 s. How many seconds pass before the third executor of branch A finishes? Supersteps are barriers and each executor starts as soon as its superstep begins.
quiz.hint: Each superstep lasts as long as its slowest executor.
quiz.explain: Superstep 1 runs A1 and B1 together and lasts max(2, 9) = 9 s. A2 runs alone in superstep 2 (2 s) and A3 in superstep 3 (2 s), so 9 + 2 + 2 = 13 s. If A's three steps were merged into one executor it would take 6 s and finish inside the same 9 s window.

quiz.q: Select every statement about checkpoint storage as a trust boundary that is true.
options: File and Cosmos storage serialize non-JSON state with pickle behind a restricted unpickler by default
Never load checkpoints from untrusted or potentially tampered sources
If pickle is unacceptable, use in-memory storage or write a custom `CheckpointStorage`
Allowing a type with `allowed_checkpoint_types` also allows module-level functions from its module
Checkpoint files are plain JSON, so reading one from any source is safe
quiz.explain: The first three are the documented position. Module-level functions and other non-type globals stay rejected even when a type is allowed, and checkpoint files can contain pickled data, so a tampered file is a code-execution risk.

quiz.q: A manager approval takes up to two days. Deploys replace the host, and the team will not pay for idle compute while waiting. The workflow runs in one process with file checkpoints. What flips the design?
options: Switch to background responses, which keep the run alive for days
Use background agents so the approval becomes a child task
Keep file checkpoints and add a loop that polls for the approval
Move to shared checkpoint storage with the request stored in the checkpoint, or host on the Durable Extension (Beta or preview) so the wait uses no compute
quiz.explain: Waiting for days across host replacement needs state that outlives the host and a way to wake the run, which shared storage or the Durable Extension provides. Background responses are a continuation token for one provider request, and in Python only for the OpenAI Responses API. Background agents lose in-flight work on restart. Polling holds compute and still depends on a local disk.

takeaways: Supersteps are barriers: parallel inside a step, wait between steps. Merge steps for truly independent paths.
A resumable workflow needs the same topology and stable executor identities, and a checkpoint store that outlives the process.
File and Cosmos checkpoint storage are a pickle-based trust boundary. Allow types explicitly, never load untrusted checkpoints, or use in-memory or custom storage.

Background responses, background agents, checkpoints and durable agents solve different problems. Only the last two survive a restart, and the durable packages are Beta or preview (checked 2026-10-13).
